architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Across at least two independent repeats, accept the dual-axis formulation as supporting H-RESIN over H-CORE if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in every repeat, which is below half of the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable is measured directly in the selected AC1920/TK100 resin-modified chemistry at 120 C and does not depend on transferring a shared thermal-response or rheological shape from the unmodified chemistry family. The audit therefore permits this direct M-HOLD-120 measurement, but the modified chemistry remains unsupported for M-ANCHOR or transferred temperature-shape claims.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-RESIN if SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61% in the matched 15-60 minute window across the measured repeats. If SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, falsify H-CORE at the declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination resolution. Results from 3.80% through 7.60% are intermediate and do not decisively separate the registered hypotheses. Because both modifier axes are active, no outcome from this experiment falsifies H-RESIN relative to H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the compositionally matched acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 experiment at 15.0% AC1920 with the same reactive-core scaling, 120 C temperature, 15-60 minute window, and at least two independent repeats; use it to test whether TK100 is required for low drift and to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over the 15-60 minute matched window
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 combines AC1920 at 15.0% and TK100 at 5.0%, leaving a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000, and directly tests viscosity-growth failure during the validated 120 C, 15-60 minute window. It offers the highest decision relevance and uncertainty reduction among the selectable cards while avoiding unsupported shared-shape transfer. A low drift result supports formulation-level superlinear suppression over reactive-core dilution, but axis attribution requires the specified acrylic-only follow-up.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120, because it is admissible under the binding audit, directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate, and is the smallest intervention in the stable tied top set. I followed the Skeptic on the interpretation: the experiment separates the dual-axis formulation from the linear-dilution prediction but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or establish a molecular mechanism. The deterministic tie was broken in favor of the smallest acrylic loading, 15.0%, while retaining the independently supported 5.0% minor-tackifier axis.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The local time-coordinate evidence contains only E1 and E5, so candidate-composition dependence of drift is largely unresolved. External modifier evidence supports the formulation region but not the exact AC1920/TK100 outcome.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: There is no temperature-shape extrapolation for the primary observable because eta_15 and eta_60 are measured directly at 120 C. Extrapolation remains high for any subsequent M-ANCHOR or shared-shape interpretation in this modified chemistry.

uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, and preparation or thermal-history variation may exceed the 2.00 percentage-point resolution; six process fields are missing.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original reactive polyurethane hot-melt formulation family represented by E1, E2, and E3, including the separately verified E1 +P chemical perturbation for thermal-shape compatibility. The intended experiment would stay inside this family only if it uses a candidate within the audited original PUR chemistry boundary; the intended matched-window hold is not justified for a chemistry-changing modifier until that boundary is audited.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence (thermal-hold drift), with the mechanism and modifier-axis dependence unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C matched-window hold shows SI_15_60 of 9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5, with E5 reaching SI_15_90 of 93.08%, demonstrating substantial isothermal viscosity growth in the local design space.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local time-coordinate evidence consists of only two original formulations, E1 and E5, measured at 120 C over 15-90 minutes with four time points. It establishes a large contrast in drift but does not resolve the candidate-composition dependence or distinguish linear dilution from superlinear suppression and tackifier dependence. By comparison, temperature response has six measured temperatures from 80-130 C across multiple runs, while realized viscosity level has repeated temperature-sweep observations, although with large E2 run spread and unknown viscosity units.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate with a matched-window 120 C thermal hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report SI_15_60 directly, without extrapolation or imputation.
Run at least two independent repeats so differences near the declared 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold can be judged.
Record enough composition information to calculate matched reactive mass fraction and identify whether the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes are active.
Include a compositionally matched comparison that can distinguish linear reactive-core dilution from superlinear resin suppression and from tackifier-required suppression.
Keep the thermal hold within the measured 120 C and 15-60 minute support; retain the full time trajectory rather than reporting only a fitted descriptor.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched measurement window, is the reduction in 120 C viscosity drift consistent with reactive-core dilution alone, substantially greater than linear dilution because of resin modification, or dependent specifically on activating the minor tackifier-like axis rather than the acrylic-like axis?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The primary observable is a direct matched-window 120 C thermal-hold drift measurement and does not rely on transferring the shared thermal-response shape from the unmodified chemistry family. Thus it remains admissible for this resin-modified chemistry, although the modified chemistry remains unsupported for M-ANCHOR-style shape transfer.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE and falsifies H-CORE at the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. Because both modifier axes are active, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction; H-DUAL is also not supported as a low-drift explanation by this outcome.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 3.80% and 7.61% indicates partial suppression but does not meet the registered superlinear-suppression criterion or decisively separate the competing hypotheses. An acrylic-only matched hold would then be required to test H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but its higher 17.5% acrylic loading adds modifier burden without increasing hypothesis discrimination or uncertainty reduction.
Deterministically tied, but its 20% acrylic loading is a larger departure from the reactive-core formulation than necessary for the same direct drift test.
Deterministically tied, but its 22.5% acrylic loading increases intervention magnitude without improving the measured information value.
Deterministically tied, but its 25% acrylic loading is the largest supported perturbation and is not needed to obtain the same separation of H-CORE from the modifier-based hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: The 120 C matched-window hold directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate, thermal-hold drift, with no model-based extrapolation. S1C41 covers both independently supported modifier axes, separates linear dilution from low-drift suppression at the registered resolution, and is the smallest sufficient intervention among the genuinely tied top cards.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C41 uses the smallest acrylic loading in the externally supported 15-25% region while retaining the independently supported 5% minor-tackifier axis. It therefore provides the minimum sufficient dual-axis intervention, limits departure from the characterized reactive core, and avoids adding modifier burden without increasing the deterministic information value.

residual_decision_risk: H-RESIN remains entangled with H-DUAL because both predict the same outcome for the dual-axis composition.
The experiment does not provide the acrylic-only counterfactual needed to test whether TK100 is required.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, and six process fields are missing; preparation and thermal-history variation may exceed the 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.
A low drift result supports a formulation-level suppression pattern but does not establish a unique molecular mechanism or modifier-axis specialization.

The modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry remains outside validated shared thermal-response support; M-ANCHOR or transferred temperature-shape interpretation would require direct verification such as M-SWEEP.
The deterministic tie is not evidence that S1C41 is scientifically correct; its selection is justified only as the smallest sufficient dual-axis intervention within the tied top set.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 activates AC1920 and TK100 simultaneously, and H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the same predicted 3.804% drift at this composition. Therefore the hold can distinguish the modifier-based predictions from H-CORE at the registered resolution, but it cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute suppression to either modifier axis. This limitation does not invalidate running S1C41 because M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved isothermal drift coordinate. An acrylic-only matched hold should be treated as the required follow-up for axis attribution, not as a reason to discard this admissible direct-drift experiment. The result must remain formulation-level and must not be reported as proof of a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied deterministic top set. The top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, the intervention-family and measurement-plan stabilities are both 1.0, and no re-weighting in the 25-scenario sweep changes the tied top set. Every recommendation_flip_boundary is null, so none of the tested 0.5x-1.5x scalings of decision relevance, extrapolation risk, hypothesis discrimination, measurement interpretability, process-state risk, or uncertainty reduction changes the decision. These perturbations are scientifically defensible as a sensitivity check, but this stability is decision stability of the transparent VOI score, not confidence or evidence that the experiment is correct. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.004583, so the numerical separation from lower cards is small even though the tied set itself is fully stable.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary observable remains inside the directly measured chemistry-independent quantity support: SI_15_60 is obtained directly at 120 C over 15-60 minutes, so no unvalidated shared thermal-response shape is reused. The resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry is outside validated support for M-ANCHOR and any transferred temperature-shape model; a direct M-SWEEP verification in that chemistry would be required before such transfer.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: Yes. M-HOLD-120 directly measures eta_15 and eta_60 at the required 120 C window, and at least two repeats are specified. The 7.61% H-RESIN falsification threshold and 3.80% low-drift threshold are both measurable relative to the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. The interpretation remains limited because rejection of H-RESIN does not uniquely prove H-CORE, and a low result cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
leakage_findings: No reliance on an unmeasured target outcome is evident in the proposed S1C41 selection; the payload explicitly states that validation identity and outcome are excluded.
The proposal risks scope leakage if its rheological result is described as establishing the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism or modifier-axis specialization, which M-HOLD-120 cannot establish.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could support either superlinear resin suppression or tackifier-required suppression; it cannot establish which modifier axis is responsible.
objections.objection: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 uses AC1920 at 15.0% and TK100 at 5.0%, so H-RESIN and H-DUAL both predict 3.804% drift. Their predicted outcomes are identical and therefore cannot be separated by SI_15_60, despite the proposer also listing all three hypotheses under "hypotheses_separated". The more specific fields correctly admit that H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment can test whether this dual-axis formulation differs from the H-CORE dilution prediction, but it cannot support the claimed axis-specific mechanism or distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
objections.objection: The composition changes both registered modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0% and TK100 is 5.0%, with the reactive core reduced to a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. Any drift change is consequently confounded between acrylic-like modification and minor-tackifier-like modification. This design cannot attribute suppression to AC1920, TK100, or their interaction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 value cannot demonstrate that TK100 is required; the tackifier-dependence claim remains untested.
objections.objection: The registered H-DUAL hypothesis predicts that acrylic addition alone remains near the linear-dilution prediction and that low drift requires a nonzero minor tackifier. S1C41 contains a nonzero minor tackifier, so it does not provide the required acrylic-only counterfactual. The proposer correctly states that an acrylic-only hold is required, but the proposed experiment itself does not test that part of H-DUAL.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No additional unsupported claim follows; the direct drift result remains interpretable as an isothermal matched-window rheological change.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 is directly calculated from eta_15 and eta_60 measured during the stated 120 C hold, with no fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This part of the proposal survives the interpretability attack.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct drift result would be weakened only if it were interpreted through an unverified temperature-shape transfer or used to justify M-ANCHOR measurements in the modified chemistry.
objections.objection: The primary M-HOLD-120 observable stays within the directly measured 120 C, 15-60 min hold-window quantity and does not reuse the unmodified-family shared thermal-response shape. The chemistry audit therefore supports its admissibility for the resin-modified candidate. However, any later M-ANCHOR reconstruction or shared-shape transfer for this AC1920/TK100 chemistry would remain unsupported; the audit marks modified chemistry as "verification_only" for shared-shape use.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could be overstated as confirming H-CORE or uniquely identifying H-RESIN when it only rejects one prediction or establishes a dual-axis formulation response.
objections.objection: The stated H-RESIN falsification criterion, SI_15_60 at or above 7.61% across at least two repeats, is attainable with M-HOLD-120 because the protocol directly records the required 15 and 60 minute viscosities and the threshold is far above the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. The criterion does not, however, identify H-CORE uniquely: a result at or above 7.61% falsifies H-RESIN but does not exclude other non-low-drift explanations, and a result below 3.80% falsifies H-CORE only under the proposal's deliberately stronger separation rule rather than the registry's general 'below linear prediction beyond resolution' wording.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A measured low drift could be incorrectly reported as proof of a molecular suppression mechanism or modifier specialization rather than as evidence for a phenomenological formulation-level hypothesis.
objections.objection: The rheological hold can establish a formulation-level drift response, but it cannot establish the molecular explanation in H-RESIN involving effective concentration and encounter frequency, nor can it establish that the minor tackifier acts on a distinct rheological coordinate. The payload's claim boundary explicitly says the hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: An apparent departure from the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction could reflect realization or process-history variation rather than modifier-induced drift suppression.
objections.objection: The M-HOLD-120 protocol has "controls_process_state": false, a process-state-risk score of 0.75, and six missing process fields. Although two independent repeats are required, the protocol does not specify enough state-control detail to ensure that between-preparation or thermal-history variation is smaller than the 2.00 percentage-point discrimination threshold.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a compositionally matched acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 experiment at the same 15.0% AC1920 loading and reactive-core scaling, with the same repeats, 120 C temperature, and 15-60 minute window. Use it alongside S1C41 to test whether the acrylic-only drift remains near the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction and whether the dual-axis result is specifically dependent on TK100. Also pre-specify process-history and state-control fields sufficient to make the 2.00 percentage-point comparison credible.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 activates both AC1920 and TK100 simultaneously, and H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the identical 3.804% prediction at this composition. The direct hold can test dual-axis suppression against H-CORE, but it cannot discriminate the two central modifier explanations or attribute the effect to either axis.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Mandatory upstream evidence: load the chemistry-provenance-audited local rheology summary and its validated chemistry boundary before ranking candidates or treating any local rheological regularity as transferable.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
